national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official portal https://www.impots.gouv.fr. Corporate registration data and business identifiers are coordinated through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is formed and registered through the INPI Guichet unique. The filing generally includes the articles of association, registered-office evidence, management identification, beneficial-owner information, capital deposit evidence, and required declarations. Following registration, the entity receives a SIREN number, a SIRET number for each establishment, an APE activity code, and tax-account details from the DGFiP. The French VAT number normally follows the format FR plus a two-digit key and the nine-digit SIREN. The entity must activate its professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr and complete the applicable tax registration questionnaire with the competent SIE. A foreign company with taxable French activities but no establishment must apply to the non-resident tax service or the competent SIE for a French VAT number. The application generally requires the foreign incorporation certificate, constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identity and authority documents, transaction and customer details, and evidence of the French taxable supplies. A business established in another EU Member State may generally use the EU administrative cooperation framework and the One Stop Shop where applicable. A business established outside the EU that is liable for French VAT generally must appoint a French fiscal representative, unless an applicable legal exception applies. VAT registration does not itself establish a permanent establishment for corporate income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A standard SARL is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS). A qualifying SARL may elect for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, or IR) if statutory conditions are satisfied, including, depending on the regime, qualifying family ownership or eligibility as a newly created company for the limited-duration start-up option. The election is subject to formal filing deadlines and eligibility conditions and is not an unrestricted check-the-box election. France has no general United States-style check-the-box regime. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework and can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or restrict relief for arrangements producing deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes. These rules do not provide a separate elective entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business, there is no general turnover threshold that permits a taxable business making ordinary taxable supplies to remain outside VAT registration; taxable supplies can require registration from commencement. The domestic franchise en base de TVA thresholds generally relevant to services are EUR 37,500 of prior-year turnover and EUR 41,250 as the tolerance threshold, subject to current statutory rules and legislative changes. The corresponding general thresholds for goods and accommodation activities are EUR 85,000 and EUR 93,500. A VPN or network-security SaaS business must analyze electronically supplied services separately. For intra-EU cross-border B2C telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronically supplied services, the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold can determine whether taxation remains in the supplier's Member State or shifts to the customer's Member State, subject to the supplier's election and the One Stop Shop rules. B2C services supplied to customers outside France may therefore require OSS or local VAT registration in the customer's jurisdiction rather than French VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through approved private platforms, known as plateformes de dématérialisation partenaires (PDPs), connected to the public directory and the DGFiP system. All French-established businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Issuance obligations apply generally to large and intermediate businesses from 1 September 2026 and to small and medium-sized businesses and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027, subject to the final statutory timetable. E-invoicing applies principally to domestic B2B transactions within the scope of French VAT; B2C and cross-border transactions are generally addressed through electronic reporting rather than the domestic B2B invoice channel. France does not operate a universal real-time pre-clearance model for all invoices. Structured invoice data, mandatory fields, transmission through an approved PDP, and electronic reporting of applicable transaction and payment data will be required. Public-sector invoices continue to use Chorus Pro. A SaaS supplier should maintain customer-status, customer-location, VAT-number validation, place-of-supply, invoice, payment, and OSS evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union can generally be exempt from French VAT, economically equivalent to zero-rating, when the supplier can prove that the goods left the EU customs territory and satisfy the documentary and supplier-status conditions. Evidence normally includes the export customs declaration, the export MRN or equivalent exit confirmation, transport evidence, commercial invoices, and accounting records. Goods supplied to VAT-registered customers in another EU Member State may qualify as exempt intra-Community supplies rather than exports, subject to valid customer VAT identification, transport evidence, recapitulative reporting, and other conditions. Offshore B2B services, including certain software and network-security services, are generally outside the scope of French VAT where the customer is a business established outside France and the place-of-supply rules allocate taxation to the customer jurisdiction; this is not technically a French 0% export rate. B2C electronically supplied services are generally taxed where the consumer is located and do not automatically qualify for export treatment. VAT refunds require a valid VAT credit, compliant invoices, accounting support, and evidence that input VAT relates to business activities. French-established taxpayers generally request refunds through their VAT returns, while eligible EU and non-EU businesses use the applicable EU electronic refund procedure or the French non-EU refund procedure, subject to reciprocity and filing requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, and export transaction
Electronic export customs declaration and export Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent proof that the goods exited the European Union
Bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, or other transport document
Packing list and, where applicable, freight-forwarder or carrier delivery evidence
Purchase order, sales contract, and accounting records linking the supply to the export
Proof of payment or other commercial settlement evidence where relevant
For intra-Community supplies: customer VAT identification evidence, transport proof, and required recapitulative statement
For offshore B2B services: customer business-status evidence, customer location evidence, contract, service records, invoice, and reverse-charge wording where applicable
Inward remittance evidence only where required by the relevant banking, contractual, or audit process; France has no universal export-VAT requirement for an inward remittance certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not impose a general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export VAT exemption or refund claims. French tax authorities may refuse or reverse the exemption or refund where the supplier cannot prove export, customer status, transport, place of supply, or transaction authenticity. The unpaid VAT may be assessed retrospectively, generally with late-payment interest at the statutory rate and tax penalties. Deliberate or fraudulent conduct can trigger a 40% penalty for deliberate breach or an 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, subject to the applicable procedural rules. Penalties may also apply for inaccurate or omitted VAT returns, invoice deficiencies, failure to transmit required transaction data, and incorrect OSS reporting. Serious VAT fraud may create criminal exposure, including fines and imprisonment for responsible individuals. Input-tax refunds can be clawed back, and repeated or material non-compliance can lead to enhanced audit activity, denial of VAT credits, joint-liability measures in applicable cases, and loss of evidentiary protection for subsequent periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is France’s central bank and part of the Eurosystem. The European Central Bank sets euro-area monetary policy. The French Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty, including the Direction générale du Trésor, administers relevant financial and external-finance rules; the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution supervises covered banks and payment institutions. French customs authorities administer applicable cash declaration requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and applies the EU single-market framework. Current-account payments and capital transfers are generally free of exchange controls, subject to EU and French sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, and reporting rules. A French SARL may generally receive and remit dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, loan repayments, and sale proceeds cross-border without prior foreign-exchange approval. Payments remain subject to corporate-law distribution and capital-maintenance rules, withholding tax where applicable, transfer-pricing requirements, treaty eligibility, beneficial-ownership checks, and bank documentary review. Dividend payments require distributable profits and valid corporate approvals; interest and royalty payments require substantiation and applicable tax analysis. Banks may request contracts, invoices, tax records, source-of-funds evidence, and payment-purpose information. Restrictions may apply to sanctioned parties, jurisdictions, or transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No general French rule requires export proceeds to be repatriated by a statutory deadline or converted into euros at a prescribed ratio. Proceeds may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to sanctions, tax, accounting, bank terms, and applicable statistical reporting. Cross-border payments and receipts may be reportable through authorized intermediaries for balance-of-payments statistics under applicable rules; the reporting party, threshold, and filing route depend on the transaction and current Banque de France requirements. Cash or bearer instruments of EUR 10,000 or more carried into or out of the EU must be declared to customs under EU cash-control rules; this is distinct from ordinary bank transfers.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for routine EUR collections, SEPA transfers, and eligible foreign-currency payments, subject to provider onboarding and supported-country coverage. An EU-licensed electronic-money institution or payment institution is not a bank: e-money is not a bank deposit and is not covered by the deposit-guarantee scheme; safeguarding applies under the provider’s regulatory regime. Verify the provider’s home-state authorization, French passporting or other lawful service basis, safeguarding arrangements, account-name and IBAN availability, limits, chargeback handling, and permitted business categories. VPN, encryption, privacy, high-volume card subscriptions, elevated refunds, and customers or counterparties in sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions may trigger enhanced review or restrictions. Maintain a French or other eligible credit-institution account for capital deposit, payroll, tax payments, and operational resilience where required or prudent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no general statutory requirement that SARL directors appear physically at a bank branch to open an account. Banks set their own onboarding procedures and may permit remote onboarding using electronic identification, certified documents, and video verification. A bank may require an in-person meeting or additional verification based on risk, foreign ownership, document origin, beneficial-ownership complexity, or its internal policy. Incorporation capital is commonly deposited with an eligible bank, notary, or other authorized depositary, with a certificate issued for registration; the account is released or converted to an operational account after registration and delivery of the required corporate documents. Confirm the provider’s current eligibility and process before relying on remote opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, layered holding companies, nominee arrangements, or difficulty identifying the ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current group organization chart to natural-person level; shareholder and beneficial-owner registers; certified incorporation and good-standing documents for relevant entities; identity and address evidence for directors, signatories, and beneficial owners; ownership and control analysis; French beneficial-ownership filing evidence; and explanations for any nominee, trust, or control arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of incorporation capital or large, rapid, or unexplained inbound transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital subscription and payment records; originating-account statements; audited financial statements or tax returns; sale, dividend, loan, or investment documents supporting source of funds and source of wealth; lender identity and loan agreement where relevant; bank remittance confirmation; and a reconciliation of the amount, sender, purpose, and corporate accounting entry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: VPN, encryption, privacy, or network-security services perceived as facilitating anonymity, sanctions evasion, cyber abuse, or restricted-jurisdiction access.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product and service description; website and terms of service; customer and geographic acceptance policy; sanctions and restricted-party screening procedures; documented prohibition and response process for unlawful use; subscription and refund flows; beneficial-ownership and merchant-processing information; data-protection and cybersecurity governance summary; and evidence that the service is a lawful commercial VPN offering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Card-processing exposure through Stripe, Paymentwall, or other acquirers, including high chargebacks, recurring billing, refunds, or mismatch between merchant, website, and account names.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed processor agreements; merchant account and settlement-account ownership evidence; transaction-flow diagram; pricing, recurring-payment consent, cancellation, refund, and chargeback policies; historical processing and dispute data if available; customer-service contacts; invoices and representative customer records; and reconciliation from processor statements to accounting records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments involving high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions, unusual intermediaries, third-party payers, or vague payment references.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying contract, invoice, purchase order, delivery or service evidence, counterparty ownership and address records, sanctions-screening results, payment-purpose explanation, intermediary rationale, and documentation linking payer, beneficiary, and contractual obligation. Reject or escalate transactions prohibited by applicable sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent corporate records, recently formed entity, virtual office, non-French directors, or inability to evidence genuine business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract or current French company-register evidence; articles of association; tax and social-security registrations as applicable; registered-office evidence; board or shareholder resolutions; director and signatory mandates; business plan; customer and supplier contracts; payroll or contractor records; and evidence of operating address and expected account activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For share capital, transfer funds from the subscriber’s own verified account to an eligible French capital-depositary account, identify the transfer as share-capital subscription or incorporation capital, and provide subscription documents and subscriber identity evidence. Obtain the capital-deposit certificate, complete registration, then provide the Kbis extract and any requested corporate records to release funds to the operational account. France has no general foreign-exchange approval or mandatory conversion requirement for ordinary equity funding. For subsequent equity injections, use the correct corporate instrument and approvals, document the subscription or premium, and record the transaction in the company’s accounts. For shareholder loans, document lender identity, principal, currency, interest, maturity, repayment terms, corporate approvals, and transfer-pricing and withholding-tax treatment. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments and SWIFT for other cross-border wires; give accurate payer, beneficiary, IBAN/BIC, purpose, and intermediary details. Do not split transfers to avoid screening or reporting. Retain bank advices, contracts, invoices, and source-of-funds evidence; the bank may request additional information or reject a transaction under legal or risk controls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer where available for euro-area and other SEPA payments. Use SWIFT customer credit transfers, commonly evidenced by MT103 or successor ISO 20022 payment data, for non-SEPA or supported foreign-currency payments; confirm beneficiary details, charges, value date, intermediary banks, and FX quote before release. For material or higher-risk supplier transactions, validate the counterparty and bank-account changes independently and retain the contract, purchase order, invoice, and evidence of service delivery. Commercial documentary letters of credit may be issued or advised by a bank subject to credit approval and UCP 600 terms; documentary collections may use URC 522. Apply sanctions screening, AML review, invoice and service substantiation, and tax and accounting controls. A VPN or SaaS supplier payment should be supported by a contract and invoice describing the service, subscription period, currency, and business purpose. Card-processor settlements and refunds should reconcile to processor reports and customer terms. No French general export-proceeds surrender rule applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for documented commercial exposures, subject to bank eligibility, suitability or appropriateness requirements where applicable, credit limits, and accurate exposure records.

Non-deliverable forwards where offered and legally available for currencies with restricted convertibility; settlement, counterparty, and product terms must be reviewed and the instrument must not be used to evade local controls.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and currency funding management, subject to bank documentation, collateral, counterparty limits, and accounting treatment.

Foreign-exchange options or collars where offered and appropriate to the company’s documented exposure, with premium, valuation, accounting, and potential MiFID II client-protection implications assessed.

Maintain a written treasury policy defining permitted instruments, counterparties, authorization limits, hedge ratios, exposure documentation, valuation, accounting, and prohibition on speculative dealing unless separately approved and legally assessed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels (annual financial statements filing to the RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval and not later than six months after fiscal year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a financial penalty of up to €3,000, a per-day coercive judicial fine (astreinte) on the managing director, and, after repeated default, administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of fiscal year-end for calendar-year companies filed electronically by mid-May (extended to the third business day after the three-month deadline)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% statutory late-filing surcharge on unpaid corporate income tax, monthly interest at 0.2%, and additional penalty up to 80% for intentional understatement or omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT reconciliation return (annual VAT summary declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed electronically by the second business day after the expiry of the calendar year for annual filers (typically early May); monthly filers submit a summarising annual declaration with their final monthly return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment incurs a 5% late-payment penalty, 0.2% monthly interest, and possible reinstatement of VAT credit claims.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office - minute book (no external filing, but recorded and kept for 10 years)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the financial year-end (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold or minute the annual meeting exposes the managing director to civil liability for mismanagement, nullification of non-approved decisions, and potential administrative penalties in the event of late accounts filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO update declaration to the RCS (beneficial owners confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Infogreffe portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; no separate annual filing, but annual review must be performed before the shareholders' meeting approving accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Knowingly filing incorrect or omitting UBO data is punishable by a fine of up to €5,000 for the company and €1,500 for the managing director; non-filing may in serious cases result in criminal sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when the SARL exceeds two of the following three thresholds: total assets ≥ €4,000,000; net turnover (before tax) ≥ €8,000,000; average employee count ≥ 50. Below these thresholds, a full audit waiver applies; shareholders representing at least one-tenth of the share capital may nonetheless request a voluntary audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) under the French Commercial Code; IFRS is mandatory only for consolidated accounts of listed groups, not for a standalone SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not require an annual UBO validation filing. The UBO initial declaration is made on incorporation and any change must be filed with the RCS within 30 days. The managing director must annually review and confirm the UBO information as part of the annual accounts approval procedure, ensuring the register is accurate and up to date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Decisions and Minutes (Registre des décisions d'associés / procès-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,200 – 18,000 per year depending on size and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first €42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover < €10m, capital held ≥75% by individuals or equivalent). R&D Tax Credit (CIR) 30% up to €100m and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII); Young Innovative Company (JEI) exemptions subject to conditions. No patent box.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no time limit; annual offset capped at €1m + 50% of taxable profit above €1m for fiscal years opened from 1 Jan 2019)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2065-SD (Impôt sur les sociétés) and annexes (2033-A to 2033-G or 2050-2059); mandatory electronic filing via impots.gouv.fr EDI-IS / EDI-TVA or approved EDI partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly advance payments (acomptes) for CIT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return: within 3 months of fiscal year-end; for 31 Dec year-end, generally by mid-May following year. Balance payment: 15th of 4th month after year-end (15 May for 31 Dec). Quarterly advance payments: 15 March, 15 June, 15 Sept, 15 Dec for 31 Dec year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax regime, consolidation status, parent company identification, and regime options.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit, extra-accounting adjustments, taxable income, and transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute CIT at 25% or treaty rate; claim foreign tax credit if any; report WHT already paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed tax adjustments and reconciliation of accounting to taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Detail extra-accounting adjustments; non-resident must document arm's length nature.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File if thresholds met; non-resident PE must comply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Treaty relief claim and certificate of residence submission.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit TRC to claim treaty WHT relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% increase; 40% if filed after formal notice; 80% if undisclosed activity. Interest for late payment: 0.20% per month (2.4% per annum). No separate daily surcharge; monthly interest applies. Late payment penalty: 5% if not paid within 30 days of notice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% for non-resident legal entities; 12.8% for non-resident individuals (excluding social levies); EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption under CGI Art. 119 ter if ≥5% holding and conditions met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Certificate of Residence (TRC) from foreign tax authority; provide to French payer before payment using form 5000-SD or equivalent; payer applies reduced treaty rate. If not provided at source, file refund claim with French tax authority before 31 Dec of second year following payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT 33.33% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents; EU Interest and Royalties Directive may exempt qualifying EU recipients; treaty rates typically 0-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File / Local File if group consolidated turnover or gross assets ≥ €400 million. Form 2257-SD filing if company turnover ≥ €50 million or group threshold met. Documentation must be available within 30 days of tax audit request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Substance is enforced through abuse of law (abus de droit, Art. L64 LPF), abnormal act of management, GAAR, and anti-treaty shopping. For SARL, French tax authority expects real office, local employees, board decisions, and risk control. Lack of substance can trigger PE recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, and 80% penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting VPN subscription revenue, using Stripe/Paymentwall accounts not reconciled to accounting, or issuing false invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741 CGI: 5 years imprisonment and €500,000 fine; aggravated (organized gang, concealed accounts) 7 years and €2,000,000. Tax adjustment plus 40% or 80% penalty and 0.20% monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De facto or de jure managers jointly liable for taxes and penalties; criminal conviction, travel ban, loss of civic rights, imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting up a French SARL with no substance to hold VPN IP or route profits to low-tax jurisdiction; artificial transfer pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Abus de droit (Art. L64 LPF): nullity of arrangement, reassessment, 80% penalty, and 0.20% monthly interest. Criminal sanctions if fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors liable for restitution, fines, and imprisonment; veil piercing under Art. L267 LPF for tax debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare Local File/Master File or Form 2257; non-arm's length royalties paid to related foreign entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: €10,000 penalty per audited year; increased to €50,000 for non-response to notice. TP adjustment taxed at 25% plus 40% penalty if abuse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers can be jointly liable for adjusted tax if fault; criminal sanctions for false documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform KYC, suspicious transaction reporting (DS), or internal AML controls while operating VPN payment rails with high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Code monétaire et financier: fines up to €1 million or 50% of illicit amounts; 5 years imprisonment for willful failure. ACPR sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for fines and imprisonment; management ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to charge and remit French VAT on B2C VPN subscriptions under OSS or non-resident VAT regime; false VAT returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% penalty for deliberate breach; 80% for hidden activity; 5 years and €500,000 under Art. 1741 CGI; 0.20% monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint liability for VAT debts under Art. L267 LPF; criminal conviction and imprisonment.
